title: General and Efficient Steering of Unconditional Diffusion Models
claim: Offline statistics and learned directions are precomputed, then reused at specific noise levels to steer sampling without gradients.
layout: 2 stacked bands (offline/inference), left-to-right, dotted colored arrows linking bands
description: The figure has two stacked gray bands, Offline on top and Inference below. In the Offline band, a white 'Labeled images' box branches into two paths. The top path goes through a cyan PCA box to a box of class and full-data statistics {μ_c, V_c}, {μ_all, V_all}. The bottom path goes through orange 'Forward noising' and 'RFM' boxes to a steering direction v_c. Dotted cyan and orange arrows run down from these outputs into the Inference band. There they feed a cyan 'Noise alignment' label (high noise) and an orange 'RFM steering' label (intermediate/late). Both sit above a gray noise-level axis from σ_T to σ_0. At the bottom, a long arrow runs from x_T ~ N to the generated image. Cyan and orange color-code the two components throughout.
caption: Overview of \method. Offline, we compute class-conditional PCA statistics (cyan) and RFM directions from forward-process activations (orange). At inference, noise alignment supplies the high-noise correction and RFM steering supplies intermediate/late activation-space control, with no classifier gradients.
abstract: Steering diffusion models toward conditions unseen during training typically requires either retraining with conditional inputs or per-step gradient computations, both of which incur substantial computational overhead. We present NA-RFM, a general recipe for efficiently steering unconditional diffusion models without gradient guidance during inference, enabling fast controllable generation. The method combines two offline-computed signals: noise alignment , a high-noise correction from PCA statistics of the target examples and the full data, and Recursive Feature Machine (RFM) activation steering , which learns a target-discriminative direction from labeled forward-process activations. During sampling, noise alignment provides coarse control at high noise, while the RFM direction is reused over intermediate/late timesteps through lightweight activation edits. Experiments on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, CelebA, and fine-grained bird species show improved target accuracy over gradient-based post-hoc guidance baselines, improved FID on the class-guidance benchmarks, and substantial inference speedups. Code: https://github.com/isotrivial/na-rfm.
